user.title: Set up HA Dev Tools MCP
user.description:
Registers a `dev_tools` LLM API for Home Assistant's native `mcp_server` integration to serve. No configuration is needed here - tools stay disarmed until you run this on the Home Assistant host (via SSH or the Terminal add-on):

`date +%s > /config/.storage/ha_dev_tools.armed`

That arms it for up to 4 hours (extended by 30 minutes on each use, idle windows beyond 30 minutes expire it). Every tool call is also checked against the calling user's admin status - see the documentation link on this integration's page for why both gates exist.

abort.single_instance_allowed: HA Dev Tools MCP is already configured. Only one instance is supported.

data_description.dry_run: When enabled, every write tool (write_automation, delete_automation, write_script, create/update/delete_helper, create/update/delete_derived_sensor, create/update/delete_template_entity, delete_entity/delete_entities, write_dashboard) is blocked - the tool call's own input is returned to the agent as a preview instead of being applied. Read-only tools and reload_domain/reload_derived_sensor/check_config are unaffected. For write_automation, delete_automation, write_script, and the template-entity tools, if git mirroring (below) is also enabled, the resolved would-be content is still pushed - to its own proposed branch (named after the write's kind and id) rather than to the mirror repo's default branch, since nothing live actually changed.
data_description.arm_idle_minutes: How long dev_tools stays armed without a tool call (5-480 minutes, default 30). Each successful call starts it again, up to the hard cap. Can't be longer than the hard cap. Applies at once, to an active arm too.
data_description.arm_max_minutes: The most dev_tools stays armed after the arm file was created, however busy (15-1440 minutes, default 240 = 4 hours). Re-arm on the host after it. Applies at once, to an active arm too.
data_description.control_excluded_devices: control_entities refuses every entity of these devices - a garage door, a door lock's relay, anything that mustn't be switched by an agent. lock, alarm_control_panel and siren entities are never controlled anyway.
data_description.control_excluded_entities: control_entities refuses these entities, whatever their device.
data_description.mirror_enabled: When enabled, a confirmed write from a supported tool (write_automation, delete_automation, write_script, create/update/delete_template_entity, write_dashboard, create/update/delete_helper, create/update/delete_derived_sensor, delete_entity/delete_entities) pushes the touched content's before/after state to the mirror repository below - a private, push-only audit trail and manual-rollback source, never the repo any deploy mechanism pulls from. Derived sensors have no real file, so their resolved config entry data/options are pushed to a synthetic path instead, and deleting one pushes a small deletion marker rather than removing anything; delete_entity works the same way, pushing the entity's full registry data to a synthetic path before removing it, since entity_registry deletion is otherwise only protected by Home Assistant's own 30-day orphan window. delete_entities pushes one combined before/after commit pair for the whole list rather than one pair per entity, so a large batch doesn't flood the mirror repository with commits. Content that looks like it contains a literal credential is never pushed. In dry-run mode (above), write_automation, delete_automation, write_script, and the template-entity tools push the resolved would-be content to a proposed branch (named after the write's kind and id) instead of the mirror repo's default branch, since nothing live changed; write_dashboard, the helper tools, the derived-sensor tools, and delete_entity/delete_entities have no such preview and push nothing while dry-run is on.
data_description.mirror_repo: A dedicated, private GitHub repository in owner/repo form. Deliberately separate from any repo a Git Pull-style add-on deploys from.
data_description.mirror_token: A fine-grained GitHub personal access token scoped to only the mirror repository above, with Contents: Read and write and nothing else - no workflow scope, no admin, an actual expiration date set. Never shown here once saved: leave it empty to keep the stored token, or enter a new one to replace it.

error.invalid_repo: Not a GitHub repository in owner/repo form.
error.idle_above_cap: The idle window can't be longer than the hard cap.

mcp_server_not_exposing_dev_tools.title: dev_tools isn't reachable over MCP yet
mcp_server_not_exposing_dev_tools.description:
HA Dev Tools registers the `dev_tools` LLM API, but Home Assistant's own **Model Context Protocol Server** integration isn't loaded or isn't configured to expose it - so an MCP client currently gets a plain 404 instead of reaching any tool here.

To fix: **Settings → Devices & Services → Add Integration → Model Context Protocol Server** (if not already added), then add `dev_tools` to its exposed APIs. This issue clears itself automatically once that's done - no restart needed.
